key_insight: AIPatient Arena shows that medical LLMs can sound strong in questioning and explanations, but still struggle with information coverage, ambiguity, and diagnostic reasoning during full consultations.
clinical_relevance: Workflow-oriented evaluation may better predict real-world clinical utility than single-turn accuracy, helping identify where medical LLMs need guardrails before deployment.
method: Built an EHR-grounded consultation framework using patient-specific knowledge graphs.
Evaluated LLMs across eight clinical competence dimensions in multi-turn physician-patient interactions.
Tested on one primary cohort and two out-of-distribution validation cohorts.
evidence_signal: The study assessed 437 primary patients plus 119 and 67 validation patients, and found high scores for questioning and professionalism but low scores for ambiguity handling, coverage, and diagnostic reasoning.
watch_item: Performance gains from richer context were limited for treatment planning, and recurrent interaction failures suggest that deployment would still need strong oversight and structured evaluation.
paper_title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
